subject: [Urgent] Accelerator-lane pricing ladder & temporary reservation hold request (Aurora Labs)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@auroralabs.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Accelerator-lane pricing ladder & temporary reservation hold request (Aurora Labs)

Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive sync this morning. Per our conversation, Aurora is looking to lock Dedicated capacity that explicitly needs the "accelerator-lane" variant (H100-LowLatency bin) for their real-time inference path. Two asks that require non-standard approval from deal desk / execs:

1) Accelerator-lane pricing ladder: Aurora wants a stepped discount that scales with committed GPU-hours across the first 6 months (15% on month 1–2, 22% month 3–4, 28% month 5–6). This deviates from our standard flat reserved discount and the lane premium.

2) Temporary reservation hold / burst terms: they need a migration window (2026-12-01 -> 2027-01-15) where we hold reservations on their account (no auto-release), and enable a burst pool for additional accelerator-lane capacity. They request capped overage during the first 60 days: $3.50 / GPU-hour capped (normally list is $5.00).

Attachments: contract redline (aurora_redline_contract_v3.pdf) and capacity plan.

Ask: can I get an exec waiver to approve the stepped discount ladder and capped overage for the first 60 days, plus the reservation soft-hold? This would be time-limited and tied to the 12-month Dedicated commitment in the SOW. I recommend: 25% one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) in lieu of deeper upfront discount, plus the stepped ladder above for months 3–6, and the capped overage for the 60-day migration window.

If approved, I will coordinate with Legal to incorporate language around the soft-hold and the overage cap into the SOW.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@auroralabs.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Procurement <procure@auroralabs.io>, Legal - Aurora <legal@auroralabs.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator-lane pricing ladder & temporary reservation hold request (Aurora Labs)

Marcus —

Appreciate the write-up and the proposed compromise. A couple of clarifying points from our side:

- The H100-LowLatency bin is a must for our real-time model path; fallback to standard H100 will cause SLA misses.
- Migration window cannot be longer than 45 days for internal release schedules; can you confirm if we can compress to 2026-12-01 -> 2027-01-15? (we actually need 46 days; ok we can work with 45)
- The stepped ladder is fine if the onboarding credit is applied and the overage cap is contractual for the first 60 days.

We will sign quickly if we can lock the soft-hold (no auto-release until 2027-01-15) and the $3.50 cap for the burst. Legal will want explicit language for our ability to request OS-level telemetry for service debug during the migration — is that ok?

Thanks — Sarah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Accelerator-lane pricing ladder & temporary reservation hold request (Aurora Labs)

Marcus / Lauren —

Looping in Jon (runtime lead) for technical Qs, and putting this up for expedited Deal Desk / Exec signoff. Key commercial ask summarized:

- Lane premium waiver + stepped discount ladder (15/22/28) for months 1–6, plus a one-time 25% onboarding credit on first invoice.
- Reservation soft-hold: hold reservations until 2027-01-15 (no auto-release).
- Overage cap: $3.50 / GPU-hour for first 60 days post-activation.

Risk notes:
- Lane premium waiver reduces unit economics materially in early months. We should require a go/no-go checkpoint at day 45 post-activation and revert to standard overage if utilization < 70% of committed rate.
- Operational ask (telemetry) needs Legal sign-off; suggest we allow scoped telemetry only for debugging and tie to an NDA addendum.

Lauren — can you confirm exec approval path? If we get green light, I will draft a short email summary for Finance & Legal to lock the SOW language.

-Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Accelerator-lane pricing ladder & temporary reservation hold request (Aurora Labs)

Karthik / Marcus —

I reviewed the commercial proposal and the numbers with Finance. Given Aurora's strategic potential and high retention probability, I approve a one-time exception with the following conditions:

1) Approve the stepped discount ladder exactly as proposed for months 1–6 (15% / 22% / 28%), conditional on a 12-month Dedicated commitment and the 25% onboarding credit applied to month 1 invoice.

2) Approve reservation soft-hold until 2027-01-15 BUT require the 45-day operational checkpoint on utilization. If utilization < 70% of committed GPU-hours at the checkpoint, overage cap is rescinded and standard overage applies going forward.

3) Approve capped overage of $3.50 / GPU-hour for the first 60 days. After day 60, revert to list overage rate unless both parties mutually agree to extend in writing.

4) Require a short addendum (Legal) that scopes telemetry to only the processes necessary for debugging the runtime during migration and that data retention for those logs is limited to 30 days. No customer PII to be included.

Jonas — please confirm the runtime team can support the lane allocation and telemetry guardrails. If you confirm, Marcus, proceed to instruct Legal to fold approved language into SOW and update HubSpot with the approved deviation.

-Lauren

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@auroralabs.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Legal - Aurora <legal@auroralabs.io>
Date: 2026-11-04T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator-lane pricing ladder & temporary reservation hold request (Aurora Labs)

Sarah —

Thanks — Lauren has approved the exception with the conditions she listed below. Jonas has confirmed readiness (runtime note attached) and Karthik will coordinate the SOW language with Legal. Action items:

- Legal (Redwood & Aurora) to add the soft-hold and overage cap language; include the 45-day utilization checkpoint and telemetry scope limitation.
- Finance to apply 25% onboarding credit to Aurora's first invoice and configure the stepped ladder for billing months 1–6.
- Marcus to schedule activation window: Provision accelerator-lane starting 2026-12-01; soft-hold in place until 2027-01-15.

I'll circulate the updated SOW for signature once Legal and Finance confirm the edits. Appreciate the quick turnaround from everyone.

Marcus
